name: Short-beaked Echidna
notes: Spiny ball with a long snout that digs for ants and termites. Often seen trundling across bush tracks on warm days.

name: Platypus
notes: Look for rings spreading on still creek pools at dawn and dusk. Dives for a minute or so, then pops up again nearby.

name: Koala
notes: Grey, round-eared marsupial wedged in a eucalypt fork. Look for droppings under trees and listen for the male's deep snoring bellow.

name: Eastern Grey Kangaroo
notes: Big grey kangaroo that grazes in mobs on open grassland and golf courses, mostly early and late in the day.

name: Common Wallaroo
notes: Stocky, shaggy-coated kangaroo of rocky hills. Dark muzzle with bare black nose; often alone on steep slopes.

name: Whiptail Wallaby
notes: Elegant pale grey wallaby with a white cheek stripe and a very long tail. Groups graze on open hillsides.

name: Red-necked Wallaby
notes: Grey wallaby with a rusty neck and shoulders and a white upper-lip stripe. Feeds at forest edges.

name: Swamp Wallaby
notes: Dark, shaggy wallaby with a yellow-orange belly. Moves with its head held low through thick undergrowth.

name: Red-necked Pademelon
notes: Small, compact rainforest wallaby with a reddish neck and short tail. Grazes on lawns beside rainforest at dusk.

name: Red-legged Pademelon
notes: Shy rainforest pademelon with rusty legs and cheeks. Thumps the ground in alarm before bolting into cover.

name: Rufous Bettong
notes: Rabbit-sized, rat-kangaroo with a grizzled coat. Hops across grassy woodland at night; builds grass nests.

name: Common Brushtail Possum
notes: Grey possum with big pointed ears and a bushy black tail. Often lives in roofs and raids fruit trees.

name: Short-eared Possum
notes: Dark, glossy brushtail with short rounded ears, found in wet forest and rainforest of the ranges.

name: Common Ringtail Possum
notes: Small possum whose white-tipped tail curls like a spring. Builds ball-shaped nests (dreys) in dense shrubs.

name: Krefft's Glider
notes: Small grey glider with a dark stripe down the back. Glides between trees and licks sap and nectar. Was called the Sugar Glider here.

name: Squirrel Glider
notes: Like a large Krefft's Glider with a fluffier, broader tail. Lives in old hollow-bearing woodland.

name: Greater Glider
notes: Big fluffy glider with large furry ears. Its eyes shine brightly in spotlight beams high in tall eucalypts.

name: Feathertail Glider
notes: Mouse-sized glider with a feather-like flattened tail. The world's smallest gliding mammal.

name: Northern Brown Bandicoot
notes: Coarse-furred bandicoot that leaves cone-shaped digging holes in lawns. Common in leafy suburbs at night.

name: Long-nosed Bandicoot
notes: Grey-brown bandicoot with a very long, pointed snout. Prefers moist forest edges.

name: Yellow-footed Antechinus
notes: Small marsupial "mouse" with orange-yellow feet and rump. Busy and bold, even by day in winter.

name: Spotted-tailed Quoll
notes: Cat-sized carnivorous marsupial with white spots that run down the tail. Rare and prized in the ranges.

name: Grey-headed Flying-fox
notes: Large fruit bat with a grey head and rusty collar. Streams out of camps at dusk to feed on blossom.

name: Black Flying-fox
notes: All-dark flying-fox, often with a reddish collar. Roosts in noisy riverside camps.

name: Little Red Flying-fox
notes: Small reddish flying-fox that arrives in huge, nomadic camps to feed on flowering eucalypts.

name: Gould's Wattled Bat
notes: Small insect-eating bat with a dark head and shoulders. One of the first to hunt at dusk, often around streetlights.

name: White-striped Free-tailed Bat
notes: Big microbat whose loud "tik-tik" calls can be heard by people. Hunts high over open country.

name: Rakali
notes: Native water-rat with a white-tipped tail and waterproof fur. Hunts crayfish and mussels along creeks and wetlands.

name: Bush Rat
notes: Native rat with soft fur and rounded ears. Shy; lives in dense rainforest and forest undergrowth.

name: Dugong
notes: Plump sea mammal that grazes on seagrass in Moreton Bay. Look for a broad back and fluke tail breaking the surface.

name: Indo-Pacific Bottlenose Dolphin
notes: Grey dolphin often seen in Moreton Bay and around Pumicestone Passage. Older adults have spotted bellies.

name: Humpback Whale
notes: Migrates past the SEQ coast from June to November. Watch for blows, breaches and tail slaps off headlands.

name: Eastern Long-necked Turtle
notes: Freshwater turtle with a neck nearly as long as its shell. Basks on logs and wanders between dams after rain.

name: Saw-shelled Turtle
notes: Creek turtle with a serrated rear shell edge and spiky neck. Common in clear streams.

name: Krefft's River Turtle
notes: The turtle of Brisbane park lakes, with a pale yellow stripe behind the eye.

name: Green Turtle
notes: Large sea turtle that grazes on seagrass in Moreton Bay. Pops its head up for a breath every few minutes.

name: Loggerhead Turtle
notes: Big-headed sea turtle that nests on Sunshine Coast and Bundaberg beaches in summer. Endangered.

name: Eastern Water Dragon
notes: Large dragon with a banded tail that basks beside creeks and leaps into the water if disturbed. Very common in city parks.

name: Eastern Bearded Dragon
notes: Spiky grey dragon that perches on posts and logs. Puffs out its dark "beard" when threatened.

name: Jacky Lashtail
notes: Small, rough-scaled grey-brown dragon with a yellow mouth lining. Basks on logs in dry forest.

name: Southern Angle-headed Dragon
notes: Well-camouflaged rainforest dragon that clings motionless to trunks. Has a spiky crest behind the head.

name: Lace Monitor
notes: Huge goanna, dark with pale bands, that climbs trees and raids picnic grounds. Give it plenty of room.

name: Eastern Blue-tongue
notes: Chunky banded lizard that flashes a bright blue tongue when threatened. A gardener's friend that eats snails.

name: Land Mullet
notes: Big glossy black skink that basks at the edges of rainforest. Crashes noisily into leaf litter when disturbed.

name: Major Skink
notes: Large brown skink with dark flecks that lives in family groups in hollow logs and rock piles.

name: Eastern Water Skink
notes: Golden-striped skink that basks on rocks beside creeks and dives into water when chased.

name: Garden Sunskink
notes: Tiny bronze skink that scuttles through every SEQ garden. Often with a pale stripe along each side.

name: Weasel Skink
notes: Small brown skink of shady, moist gardens and rainforest with a white mark behind the eye.

name: Robust Velvet Gecko
notes: Big velvety native gecko with a pale zigzag pattern. Hunts insects on tree trunks and house walls at night.

name: Burton's Legless Lizard
notes: Snake-like lizard with a wedge-shaped snout and visible ear holes. Hunts skinks; harmless to people.

name: Carpet Python
notes: Non-venomous python with a variable blotched pattern. Often found in roofs and backyard trees, where it eats rats.

name: Common Tree Snake
notes: Slender green, blue or black snake with a yellow belly. Climbs fast and is not dangerous to people.

name: Keelback
notes: Olive-brown snake with keeled scales that hunts frogs near water, including cane toads. Not dangerous.

name: Red-bellied Black Snake
notes: Glossy black snake with a red-pink belly edge, often near water. Venomous: watch from a distance.

name: Eastern Brown Snake
notes: Fast, plain brown snake of paddocks and suburbs. Highly venomous: keep well away and never try to catch it.

name: Yellow-faced Whipsnake
notes: Slender grey snake with a pale ring around large eyes. Hunts skinks by day. Venomous: watch from a distance.

name: Eastern Small-eyed Snake
notes: Shiny black snake with a pinkish belly that hides under logs by day. Venomous: don't handle.

name: Brown Tree Snake
notes: Banded rear-fanged snake with large eyes that hunts birds at night. Mildly venomous; not considered dangerous.

name: Green Tree Frog
notes: Plump green frog that lives in downpipes and water tanks. Calls a deep "crawk crawk" after summer rain.

name: Eastern Dwarf Tree Frog
notes: Tiny green or brown frog of reeds and lily pads. Its insect-like "wreek, pip-pip" fills wetlands on warm nights.

name: Graceful Tree Frog
notes: Slim bright-green frog with orange thighs and a golden eye. Calls a long, drawn-out "aaarrk" from shrubs near water.

name: Bleating Tree Frog
notes: Fawn frog with a dark stripe down each side. Its piercing bleat is one of the loudest frog calls after rain.

name: Leaf-green Tree Frog
notes: Slender green frog with a gold-edged dark stripe through the eye. Calls a soft "rrrrk" beside rainforest creeks.

name: Naked Tree Frog
notes: Plain fawn-grey frog with a dark band through the eye. Long, grating trill in open woodland after rain.

name: Emerald-spotted Tree Frog
notes: Grey-brown frog with tiny emerald flecks and a cross-shaped pupil. Its call sounds like a maniacal cackle.

name: Stony Creek Frog
notes: Creek-side frog with a dark stripe through the eye. Breeding males turn lemon-yellow.

name: Rocket Frog
notes: Long-legged, pointy-nosed frog that leaps huge distances. Calls a rapid "wick-wick-wick" from grassy swamps.

name: Cascade Tree Frog
notes: Small, variable rainforest frog of fast rocky streams in the ranges. Listed as a species of concern.

name: Striped Marsh Frog
notes: Brown frog with dark stripes and a pale mid-back line. Its single "tok" call is heard from garden ponds all year.

name: Spotted Grass Frog
notes: Spotted grey-green frog that calls a rapid machine-gun "uk-uk-uk" from flooded grass.

name: Scarlet-sided Pobblebonk
notes: Big burrowing frog with red patches on its sides. Calls a resonant "bonk" after heavy summer rain.

name: Salmon-striped Frog
notes: Striking frog with salmon-pink stripes on a brown back. Lives in grassland and floodplain swamps.

name: Ornate Burrowing Frog
notes: Squat, patterned frog that stays buried in sandy soil until storms. Calls a short "unk" from temporary pools.

name: Tusked Frog
notes: Warty brown frog with a red-and-black marbled belly. Males have two small tusks in the lower jaw.

name: Great Barred Frog
notes: Big, long-legged frog with barred legs that hunts on rainforest floors. Calls a deep "wark".

name: Beeping Froglet
notes: Tiny froglet with a sheep-like "eeeek" call from shallow pools, mostly in the cooler months.

name: Common Eastern Froglet
notes: Tiny, variable froglet. A chorus of its "crick-crick-crick" calls comes from wet ditches in winter.

name: Wallum Froglet
notes: Tiny froglet of acid wallum swamps on the coastal lowlands. Vulnerable; calls a tinkling "tching".

name: Richmond Birdwing
notes: Huge black-and-green birdwing of lowland rainforest. Breeds only on native birdwing vine. Vulnerable.

name: Orchard Swallowtail
notes: Large black-and-white swallowtail; females have red and blue spots. Lays eggs on citrus trees.

name: Blue Triangle
notes: Fast black butterfly with a band of electric-blue triangles. Rarely settles except to sip from flowers.

name: Macleay's Swallowtail
notes: Green-and-black swallowtail with long tails, mostly seen in mountain rainforest.

name: Pale Triangle
notes: Black butterfly with rows of pale green triangles. Often drinks at damp ground with other butterflies.

name: Chequered Swallowtail
notes: Tailless swallowtail with a chequered black-and-cream pattern. Breeds on native citrus-family herbs inland.

name: Clearwing Swallowtail
notes: Males have clear, glassy wings with red and black spots. Flies slowly over open woodland.

name: Caper White
notes: White butterfly with heavy black edges. Huge migrating swarms pass through in spring and summer.

name: Common Grass Yellow
notes: Small lemon-yellow butterfly with black wing edges that flutters low over lawns and grass.

name: Lemon Migrant
notes: Fast pale lemon or white butterfly. Big numbers migrate through gardens in summer and autumn.

name: Black Jezebel
notes: Black-and-white jezebel with red and yellow spots underneath. Larvae feed on mistletoe.

name: Scarlet Jezebel
notes: Underwings have a bright scarlet band and yellow spots. Feeds high in flowering trees.

name: Imperial Jezebel
notes: Black-and-white with bright red patches underneath. Mostly seen in winter and spring.

name: Caper Gull
notes: White or yellowish butterfly with black borders that breeds on native caper trees.

name: Lesser Wanderer
notes: Smaller orange cousin of the Monarch, with black veins and white spots on the wingtips.

name: Blue Tiger
notes: Black butterfly with pale blue streaks and spots. Gathers in winter clusters in sheltered gullies.

name: Common Crow
notes: Dark brown butterfly with white spots on the edges. Slow, gliding flight; often in gardens.

name: Varied Eggfly
notes: Males are velvet black with purple-ringed white spots; females are brown and variable.

name: Evening Brown
notes: Leaf-brown butterfly with eyespots that flies at dusk and rests on the ground among leaf litter by day.

name: Meadow Argus
notes: Brown butterfly with big blue-and-orange eyespots. Basks on bare ground with wings open.

name: Australian Painted Lady
notes: Orange-and-black butterfly with blue-centred eyespots on the hindwings. Migrates in spring.

name: Glasswing
notes: Slow-flying butterfly with clear forewings and a cream hindwing edged with black spots.

name: Dingy Bush-brown
notes: Plain brown butterfly with small eyespots underneath that flits low through grassy forest edges.

name: Tailed Emperor
notes: Powerful flier with twin tails on each hindwing. Attracted to fermenting fruit and sap.

name: Australian Rustic
notes: Orange-and-brown butterfly with a dark wingtip that glides around rainforest edges.

name: Common Grass-blue
notes: Tiny lilac-blue butterfly that flutters just above lawns everywhere.

name: Fiery Jewel
notes: Small butterfly with brilliant metallic orange-red and green patterns underneath. Tended by ants.

name: Satin Azure
notes: Shimmering blue butterfly whose larvae feed on mistletoe.

name: Long-tailed Pea-blue
notes: Small brownish-blue butterfly with tiny tails and eyespots, often around flowering peas.

name: Imperial Hairstreak
notes: Pale blue butterfly with black-and-orange tails. Colonies cluster on young wattles, tended by ants.

name: Regent Skipper
notes: A stunning black-and-yellow skipper with a red body, found around rainforest margins.

name: Orange Palm-dart
notes: Darting orange skipper that breeds on palms in suburban gardens.

name: Spotted Gum
notes: Tall gum with smooth, dimpled bark in patches of grey, cream and pink. Flowers in winter and feeds lorikeets.

name: Scribbly Gum
notes: Smooth white bark covered in squiggly "scribbles" made by moth larvae. Common on sandy soils.

name: Forest Red Gum
notes: Smooth blotched bark and long horn-shaped buds. A key koala food tree.

name: Grey Ironbark
notes: Hard, deeply furrowed dark grey bark. Its very dense timber was prized for bridges.

name: Pink Bloodwood
notes: Rough, flaky bark and red sap that oozes from wounds. Masses of cream flowers in summer.

name: Tallowwood
notes: Soft, fibrous orange-brown bark. Leaves are a favourite koala food.

name: Swamp Mahogany
notes: Spongy red-brown bark in coastal swamps. Winter nectar feeds flying-foxes and honeyeaters.

name: Brush Box
notes: Smooth salmon-pink upper bark with rough lower trunk. Widely planted as a street tree.

name: Broad-leaved Paperbark
notes: Layered papery white bark and creamy bottlebrush flowers. Forms swamp forests.

name: Weeping Bottlebrush
notes: Drooping branches covered in red bottlebrush flowers that attract honeyeaters.

name: Coastal Banksia
notes: Pale yellow flower spikes and leaves silvery underneath. Grows on dunes and headlands.

name: Wallum Banksia
notes: Thick serrated leaves and fat greenish-yellow cones. A wallum heath icon.

name: Brisbane Wattle
notes: Soft, narrow leaves and masses of pale yellow ball flowers in late winter.

name: Early Black Wattle
notes: Golden flower spikes appear from mid-winter. Common in open forest.

name: Moreton Bay Fig
notes: Huge spreading fig with buttress roots and large glossy leaves. Its figs feed many birds and flying-foxes.

name: Hoop Pine
notes: Tall conifer with tufted branches poking above the rainforest canopy, and bark that peels in hoops.

name: Bunya Pine
notes: Dome-shaped conifer with sharp leaves. Its huge cones fall in summer and were a traditional feast food.

name: Macadamia
notes: The native Queensland nut tree, with spiky-edged leaves and dangling cream flower spikes.

name: Blue Lilly Pilly
notes: Glossy leaves and fluffy cream flowers followed by purple-blue fruit that birds love.

name: Black Bean
notes: Bright red-and-orange pea flowers in summer, then large bean pods. Grows along rivers.

name: Illawarra Flame Tree
notes: Drops its leaves and covers itself in scarlet bell flowers in early summer.

name: Piccabeen Palm
notes: Graceful palm of wet gullies with lilac flowers and bright red fruit.

name: Cabbage Tree Palm
notes: Tall fan palm with round, deeply divided leaves on a slim trunk.

name: Red Cedar
notes: Deciduous rainforest giant whose new spring leaves glow red-pink. Heavily logged last century.

name: Firewheel Tree
notes: Red-and-orange flowers arranged like the spokes of a wheel. Loved by nectar-feeding birds.

name: Native Frangipani
notes: Sweetly scented cream flowers that turn yellow as they age.

name: Silky Oak
notes: Fern-like leaves and brilliant golden-orange flower combs in late spring.

name: Grey Mangrove
notes: Mangrove with grey-green leaves and pencil-like breathing roots (pneumatophores) poking from the mud.

name: Pandanus
notes: Coastal screw pine with stilt roots, spiralling leaves and a pineapple-like fruit.

name: Coastal She-oak
notes: Drooping, needle-like branchlets that sigh in the sea breeze. Grows on dunes.

name: Swamp She-oak
notes: She-oak of estuaries and tidal flats. Glossy black-cockatoos feed on its cones.

name: Beach Spinifex
notes: Silvery grass that binds sand dunes. Its spiky seed heads roll along the beach in the wind.

name: Cottonwood
notes: Coastal hibiscus with heart-shaped leaves and yellow flowers that turn red as they fade.

name: Grass Tree
notes: Dark trunk topped with a skirt of fine grassy leaves and a tall flower spike after fire.

name: Native Violet
notes: Low creeping plant with kidney-shaped leaves and small purple-and-white flowers.

name: Kangaroo Grass
notes: Tussock grass with rusty-red seed heads in summer. A key native pasture grass.

name: Blue Flax Lily
notes: Strappy leaves with sprays of small blue star flowers, followed by shiny blue berries.

name: Purple Coral Pea
notes: Twining vine covered in purple pea flowers in late winter.

name: Dusky Coral Pea
notes: Strong climber with large dark-red pea flowers.

name: Elkhorn Fern
notes: Fern that grows on trees and rocks, with a shield of brown leaves and forked "elkhorn" fronds.

name: Rough Tree Fern
notes: Tree fern with a rough, stubbly trunk and large lacy fronds, in wet gullies.

name: Bird's Nest Fern
notes: Large glossy fronds arranged in a nest-shaped rosette high in rainforest trees.

name: Pink Rock Orchid
notes: Small orchid on rocks with sprays of fragrant pink-mauve flowers in late winter.

name: King Orchid
notes: Large orchid on rocks and trees with long sprays of cream-yellow flowers.
